sentence: The committee has been grappling with the implications of the new regulation
explanation: 'Grapple with' significa lidiar con un tema complejo. Presente perfecto continuo para un esfuerzo en curso.

sentence: Not only did the report gloss over the key findings but it also misrepresented the data
hint: Inversion after 'Not only': Not only + auxiliary + subject
explanation: 'Gloss over' significa tratar algo de manera superficial. 'Not only...but also' con inversión para dar énfasis.

sentence: Had the researchers not stumbled upon the anomaly the discovery would never have been made
hint: Inverted conditional: Had + subject + not + past participle
explanation: 'Stumble upon' significa descubrir algo por accidente. Tercer condicional invertido sin 'if'.

sentence: The professor urged the students to delve into the primary sources more thoroughly
explanation: 'Delve into' significa investigar a fondo. 'Urged someone to' + forma base.

sentence: Seldom does the board touch on such controversial matters in public sessions
explanation: 'Touch on' significa mencionar brevemente. El adverbio negativo 'seldom' provoca inversión sujeto-auxiliar.

sentence: The government is cracking down on tax evasion with unprecedented measures
explanation: 'Crack down on' significa tomar medidas estrictas contra algo. Presente continuo para una política actual.

sentence: Were the company to phase out the legacy system productivity would initially drop
hint: Formal conditional: Were + subject + to + base form
explanation: 'Phase out' significa eliminar gradualmente. 'Were...to' es una estructura condicional formal.

sentence: The author draws on extensive fieldwork to substantiate her argument
explanation: 'Draw on' significa usar algo como recurso. Con 'the author' (singular), se usa 'draws'.

sentence: Never before had the institution embarked on such an ambitious undertaking
hint: Inversion after 'Never before': Never before + had + subject
explanation: 'Embark on' significa emprender un proyecto importante. 'Never before' provoca inversión.

sentence: The panel called for a comprehensive overhaul of the existing framework
explanation: 'Call for' significa exigir o requerir. Pasado simple para una acción completada.

sentence: The report fails to account for the recent budget shortfall
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Account for' significa explicar la causa de algo.

sentence: The reforms are expected to bring about significant change
hint: Subject + passive verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Bring about' significa causar que algo suceda.

sentence: Researchers carried out an extensive review of the literature
explanation: 'Carry out' significa realizar una tarea. Es separable: 'carried an extensive review out' también es correcto.

sentence: The committee has not ruled out further investigation
hint: Subject + auxiliary + negative + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Rule out' significa descartar. Es separable: 'ruled further investigation out' también es correcto.

sentence: The auditors singled out three departments for closer scrutiny
hint: Subject + phrasal verb + object + prepositional phrase
explanation: 'Single out' significa seleccionar de un grupo. Es separable: 'singled three departments out' también es correcto.

sentence: New employees often struggle to get to grips with the software
hint: Subject + adverb + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Get to grips with' significa empezar a comprender y manejar algo complejo.

sentence: The new evidence sheds light on the cause of the incident
explanation: 'Shed light on' significa aclarar o explicar algo.

sentence: It took her years to come to terms with the loss
hint: It + verb + object + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Come to terms with' significa aceptar algo difícil emocionalmente.

sentence: The committee will weigh up the pros and cons before deciding
hint: Subject + modal + phrasal verb + object + time clause
explanation: 'Weigh up' significa sopesar o evaluar cuidadosamente. Es separable.

sentence: The film failed to live up to expectations
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Live up to' significa estar a la altura de algo esperado.
